assembly_instructions: 1. Print the Nylon-12 palm tray floor, side rails, rear wall, front finger crossmember, four standoffs, four base flexures, twelve finger links, and eight compliant interphalangeal flexure webs. 2. Bolt the dark anodized aluminum wrist connector to the rear wall through the brushed-steel flange disk using the four visible M3 flange bolt heads, then fasten the rear wall to the tray. 3. Install the 22 mm geared DC motor, gearbox cap, and 14 mm brass drive spool in the open tray, with the spool axis running across the hand width. 4. Mount the floating pulley tree with the primary yoke near the spool, the first-stage pulley in the yoke, the two second-stage pulleys forward and outboard, and four guide eyelets at the front crossmember. 5. Attach the four proximal links to their base flexures, then install the middle and distal links in the shown inward-curled posture so the inner fingers wrap around the 32 mm sample cylinder. 6. Route the main Spectra line from the spool to the primary pulley, split it to the two second-stage pulleys, then route four tendons through the guide eyelets along the underside of each finger to the distal anchor pads. 7. Tension all four tendons equally, tie off at the four black anchor pads, and verify the floating pulleys equalize when one finger contacts first. 8. Leave the cover plate offset above and behind the palm for inspection, or lower it onto the four standoffs and secure it with the four cover screw heads after testing free motion.

info.japanese_name: イェール OpenHand モデルT
info.summary: Open-source, tendon-driven, underactuated four-fingered robotic hand from Yale's GRAB Lab. Single actuator drives all fingers through a floating pulley tree for adaptive grasping.
info.description: The Model T is part of the Yale OpenHand Project — a family of open-source, low-cost, 3D-printed robotic hands designed by Aaron Dollar's GRAB Lab at Yale. Model T uses a 2+2 pincer arrangement of four underactuated fingers; all four are driven from a single DC motor through a floating pulley tree that equalizes tendon tension. Because the pulley tree is mechanically floating, tendons equalize tension across the fingers — when one finger contacts an object, the others keep closing until they too make contact, producing a conformal grasp without any sensing. Finger joints are printed Nylon-12 flexure hinges rather than discrete pin joints, which drops the parts count and makes the whole hand robust to impact. All CAD, BOM, and build instructions are released under CC BY-NC 3.0 and have seeded dozens of academic variants.
info.operator: Yale GRAB Lab + the academic robotics community
info.contractor: Aaron Dollar / Yale GRAB Lab (OpenHand Project)
info.contract_date: OpenHand Project launched 2013; Model T widely built 2014 onward
info.contract_value: ≈US$500 in parts (one motor + printed shells + Spectra tendon)
info.status: Open-source, widely replicated in research labs

facts.label: Fingers
facts.value: 4 fingers in a 2+2 pincer layout; each finger has 3 visible links, 1 base flexure, and 2 printed interphalangeal flexure webs.

facts.label: Joints
facts.value: Printed Nylon-12 compliant flexures replace pin joints at all 8 interphalangeal bends plus 4 base flexures.

facts.label: Actuation
facts.value: 1 geared DC motor drives a 14 mm spool feeding a two-stage floating pulley tree and 4 Spectra tendons.

facts.label: Pulley equalization
facts.value: 1 primary floating pulley and 2 second-stage floating pulleys split one motor stroke into four tendon branches.

facts.label: Approximate envelope
facts.value: 0.24 m long including wrist connector, 0.12 m wide across outer fingers, and about 0.13 m high with the offset exploded cover shown.

facts.label: Palm tray
facts.value: Open tray about 0.14 m × 0.11 m × 0.018 m with separate rails, rear wall, crossmember, and standoffs instead of a closed shell.

facts.label: Sample object
facts.value: Grasp demonstrator is a 0.032 m diameter cylinder centered between the two inner distal fingertips.

facts.label: Fasteners
facts.value: 4 cover screws and 4 wrist flange bolts are shown as separate heads so the service and mounting interfaces are buildable.

facts.label: License
facts.value: CC BY-NC 3.0 for OpenHand CAD and documentation.

parts.name: Open Palm Tray Floor
parts.role: Nylon-12 floor plate supports the motor, pulley tree, rails, and finger crossmember while leaving the actuator bay open for inspection.

parts.name: Palm Side Rail Port
parts.role: Port-side printed rail stiffens the open palm tray without covering the motor or tendon routing.

parts.name: Palm Side Rail Starboard
parts.role: Starboard-side printed rail mirrors the port rail and keeps the tray rectangular while preserving a visible cutaway center.

parts.name: Rear Wrist Wall
parts.role: Rear printed wall carries the wrist connector loads into the open palm tray.

parts.name: Front Finger Crossmember
parts.role: Front printed crossmember anchors the four finger-base flexures and the tendon guide eyelets.

parts.name: Cover Standoff Port Rear
parts.role: Rear port spacer sets the cover height and shows where the removable top plate bolts down.

parts.name: Cover Standoff Port Front
parts.role: Front port spacer supports the removable cover without obscuring the tendon guides.

parts.name: Cover Standoff Starboard Rear
parts.role: Rear starboard spacer mirrors the port standoff and makes the cover mounting pattern buildable.

parts.name: Cover Standoff Starboard Front
parts.role: Front starboard spacer completes the four-point cover support pattern.

parts.name: Palm Cover Plate (Offset Exploded)
parts.role: Removable printed cover is offset above and behind the palm so the motor, spool, and pulley tree remain visible in the ISO render.

parts.name: Cover Screw Head Port Rear
parts.role: Visible screw head marks the rear port cover fastener location when the exploded plate is lowered onto the standoff.

parts.name: Cover Screw Head Port Front
parts.role: Visible screw head marks the front port cover fastener location when the exploded plate is lowered onto the standoff.

parts.name: Cover Screw Head Starboard Rear
parts.role: Visible screw head marks the rear starboard cover fastener location when the exploded plate is lowered onto the standoff.

parts.name: Cover Screw Head Starboard Front
parts.role: Visible screw head marks the front starboard cover fastener location when the exploded plate is lowered onto the standoff.

parts.name: Cylindrical Wrist Connector
parts.role: Robot-arm adapter cylinder bolts to the rear wall and defines the mounting axis behind the palm.

parts.name: Wrist Flange Face
parts.role: Thin flange disk spreads wrist adapter clamp loads into the rear printed wall.

parts.name: Wrist Flange Bolt Top
parts.role: Top M3 bolt head clamps the wrist flange into the rear wall.

parts.name: Wrist Flange Bolt Bottom
parts.role: Bottom M3 bolt head completes the vertical clamp pair on the wrist flange.

parts.name: Wrist Flange Bolt Port
parts.role: Port-side M3 bolt head locates the wrist flange against torsion from grasp loads.

parts.name: Wrist Flange Bolt Starboard
parts.role: Starboard-side M3 bolt head mirrors the port fastener and completes the four-bolt wrist pattern.

parts.name: Geared DC Motor Can
parts.role: Single geared DC motor provides the only powered input for all four underactuated fingers.

parts.name: Motor Gearbox Cap
parts.role: Compact gearbox cap reduces motor speed and increases torque before the tendon spool.

parts.name: Tendon Drive Spool
parts.role: Grooved spool winds the primary Spectra line that pulls the floating pulley tree forward.

parts.name: Primary Floating Pulley Yoke
parts.role: Free yoke carries the first pulley and floats so motor force self-equalizes before splitting left and right.

parts.name: Primary Floating Pulley Wheel
parts.role: First pulley redirects the motor tendon into the two second-stage branches.

parts.name: Second-Stage Pulley Port Pair
parts.role: Port-side second-stage pulley divides one branch into the two port-side finger tendons.

parts.name: Second-Stage Pulley Starboard Pair
parts.role: Starboard-side second-stage pulley divides one branch into the two starboard-side finger tendons.

parts.name: Main Motor Tendon Loop
parts.role: Spectra line from the drive spool to the primary floating pulley transmits the motor stroke.

parts.name: Port Split Tendon
parts.role: Short Spectra branch links the primary pulley to the port second-stage pulley.

parts.name: Starboard Split Tendon
parts.role: Short Spectra branch links the primary pulley to the starboard second-stage pulley.

parts.name: Tendon Guide Eyelet F1
parts.role: Low-friction eyelet at the crossmember aligns finger 1 tendon with its underside groove.
